entities.summary:
Antonio Urceo, called Codro, was an Italian humanist and grammar teacher in Bologna, active during the late 15th century.


He was a key figure in the revival of classical learning in Italy, and his teachings had a lasting impact on the development of the Italian language and literature.


Urcio's work was heavily influenced by the ancient Greeks and Romans, and he sought to revive their classical ideals in a Christian context. He was particularly interested in the study of rhetoric and the art of eloquence, and his own writings on these subjects were widely read and admired during his lifetime.
